result.title: Eliciting Research Taste in LLMs through Future Research Direction Choice
result.comment: Accepted at the LM4Sci Workshop at COLM 2026. 23 pages, 7 figures, 18 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/Lossfunk/research-taste-eval-v1
result.summary: Research taste is increasingly discussed in the context of AI scientists, yet remains little studied or measured in LLMs. This judgment matters especially in open-ended research, where a direction must be chosen before a verifiable objective is available. We operationalize research taste through one task of the scientific workflow: choosing which future research direction to pursue given a research goal and current results. Rather than predicting downstream scientometric metrics or treating author choices as objectively correct, we evaluate models against human-authored future-work directions and report author alignment, stable divergence, and unstable choice as behavioral measures of research-direction preference. We construct an order-controlled evaluation of 80 pairwise comparisons from 19 ML papers published between December 2025 and February 2026 across four subdomains. Each query presents a research goal, hypotheses tested with key results, and two candidate future directions: one author-recommended direction and one plausible distractor sampled from a similar paper. Across eight LLMs, author alignment ranges from 45.0% to 67.5%, while stable divergence ranges from 15.0% to 36.2%. These divergences largely persist under similarity controls, prompt ablations, and an author-preference framing check, and inter-model agreement suggests that some non-author preferences are shared across models. We characterize what models diverge toward using transition-category labels and selected reasoning examples, finding recurring movement toward scaling/generalization and trade-offs between methodological and infrastructure/data extensions. We view this as an early descriptive evaluation for eliciting research taste profiles in LLMs, and as a step toward understanding and steering their research preferences as they take on more autonomous roles in novel open-ended scientific discovery.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「research taste」操作化为一个任务：给定研究目标与已有假设、关键结果，让模型在两条候选未来方向中择一；基于 19 篇 ML 论文构建 80 组顺序控制的成对比较，对 8 个 LLM 报告作者对齐率、稳定分歧与不稳定选择等行为指标，并刻画模型偏好偏向 scaling/泛化等类别。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「在尚无客观可验证目标时做方向选择」并区分稳定偏好与随机波动的测量方式，可能为 LVR 中「继续思考、换推理路径还是停止」这类元决策及模型策略偏好的刻画提供评价思路，但材料不含视觉、latent 状态成分，联系需较多核查。
